analysis:
Both changed files, docs/architecture/inference.md and docs/developer/test.md, are documentation only. No code, configuration or control change is visible. Reviewed units cover the head text of inference.md (lines 1621-1794, which do not include the changed hunk at head lines 790-806), the patch for test.md and its base text. The inference.md patch excerpt was read in file_changes.

The docs describe a prompt-token cache (PromptTokenCache in LocalTokenizerBridge) that reuses token IDs of pieces seen before, scoped to the prefix-cache scope. They state:
- Reuse never crosses a cache scope.
- Tokenizers or templates outside the stated conditions, or failing a load-time comparison, keep the unchanged path.
- Sampled background comparisons disable reuse on a mismatch.
- DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0 restores the unchanged path.

This is a possible new in-memory cross-request timing or reuse surface adjacent to T-041 (the TTFT oracle, SEC-035). The documented scope-bound reuse is consistent with T-041's coordinator-authored cacheSalt isolation, so the docs do not widen the accepted channel on their own. The implementation, which is not in the supplied evidence, must verify the following (the PromptTokenCache source and ChatTemplateLoopRewrites are not supplied):
- The cache keys on the cacheSalt or scope.
- The cache is bounded in size.
- The cache is purged on scope or model change.
- Rendered prompt text or token IDs are not persisted to disk or logged.
- Memory is bounded for the up-to-four-core parallel encode.

The test.md additions only describe synthetic tests and an opt-in PROMPT_TOKEN_CACHE_MODEL_DIRS env var for local model directories. They add no secrets and no production endpoints. The benchmark --prompt-prep CLI is local-only and loads only the tokenizer.

No security regression is visible. Recommend that the threat model, specifically T-041, be updated or reviewed when the PromptTokenCache implementation lands, to record the in-memory token-ID cache's scope isolation and lifetime.
